Mold Testing & Lab Results
Independent lab results documenting mold conditions at 3620 Duckhorn Dr #1003, Sacramento CA. Each event is marked on the humidity timeline. The humidity readings on and before each test date provide environmental context for the lab findings.
Lab Verdict
Elevated Mold Confirmed
Independent tests: Sep 5 & Nov 12
September 5, 2025
Initial Mold Inspection & Lab Testing Elevated — Remediation Required
MI&T Environmental Testing Group · Microbial Express Labs (AIHA EMLAP #288327) · Lab Ref: 1622090825033-M
Kids Bedroom (Air)345,960 spores/m³ — Aspergillus/Penicillium 100% of total. Outdoor control: 680 spores/m³. Indoor count was 509× higher than outdoor baseline. Critical
Kids Mattress (Swab)Aspergillus/Penicillium confirmed Heavy (H) — 1,001–10,000 spores. General Impression: Fungal Growth (FG). Item non-salvageable. FG Confirmed
Patio Control (Air)Stachybotrys (black mold water damage indicator) detected outdoors. 680 spores/m³ total — normal outdoor baseline.
Visual FindingsExtensive visible mold on floor, mattress, headboard, toys, backpacks, shoes, Legos, hats, pictures. Wall moisture 45–90%. HVAC register moisture elevated.
Inspector NotesSource identified as humidity issue. Professional remediation required. Mattress and all porous belongings to be discarded. HVAC evaluation recommended.
Humidity at time of test: Sep 5, 2025 — checking sensor data…
The kids' bedroom air contained spore levels 509 times higher than the outdoor control — a finding consistent with sustained indoor humidity above 70% for weeks prior. Aspergillus/Penicillium thrive at relative humidity above 65% and can colonize porous materials within 24–48 hours of sustained exposure.
October 20, 2025
Post-Remediation Clearance Test — Property Initiated Declared Clear
Adam Labs Inc. · Sacramento, CA · Client: RMC (Property Management) · Lab Director: Adam Jahnsen, CMC
Overall FindingDeclared "normal conditions" and "fit for occupancy." Limited air investigation — compared indoor areas to an outdoor reference sample only. No surface sampling of HVAC components conducted.
Who CommissionedThis test was ordered and paid for by RMC (property management), not by the occupant. The occupant did not receive the data or participate in the sampling process.
What Was Not TestedThe A/C intake — where active mold growth was confirmed 23 days later — was not swabbed or sampled during this clearance visit.
Context: Oct 20, 2025 is outside the current sensor monitoring window. Sensor data begins Mar 11, 2026. Conditions at the time of this test are not captured in this dataset.
This clearance is directly refuted by the November 12 independent test. An independent lab commissioned 23 days later confirmed active mold growth in the HVAC A/C intake — a location not sampled during this visit. The property's own clearance test used air sampling only, which will not detect mold actively growing inside ductwork or on intake surfaces. The sequence — property-commissioned clearance → independent test finds active growth — is documented in the record below.
November 12, 2025
Independent Post-Remediation Clearance Test Active Mold — A/C Intake
Nation Laboratories (Gold River, CA) · Client: Bio Safety Clean · Project ID: NL-6024210
Bedroom (Air)160 spores/m³ — Normal. Below outdoor comparison. Normal
Bathroom (Air)490 spores/m³ — Penicillium/Aspergillus (133 spores/m³), Ascospores (160), elevated debris. Elevated
A/C Intake (Swab)Cladosporium (Low-Moderate), Nigrospora (Rare), Ulocladium (Rare), Hyphae Fragments. General Impression: Mold Growth Confirmed. Active Growth
Outside Control4,200 spores/m³ — Cladosporium dominant (1,707), Ascospores (1,733), Basidiospores (400). Normal outdoor profile.
Context: Nov 12, 2025 is outside the current sensor monitoring window. Sensor data begins Mar 11, 2026. The finding of active mold in the A/C intake suggests the humidity-driven conditions enabling growth persisted through and beyond the remediation period.
Despite the bedroom air testing normal, active mold growth was confirmed inside the A/C intake — the component that circulates air throughout the entire unit. Cladosporium and Ulocladium in an HVAC intake indicates the moisture source was not fully resolved by remediation. Ulocladium is a water damage indicator mold rarely found in dry environments.
Documentation Summary
Three lab events are documented at 3620 Duckhorn Dr #1003. The September 5 independent test confirmed critical mold contamination — airborne spore counts 509× above outdoor baseline with surface-confirmed fungal growth on the mattress. The October 20 property-initiated clearance (commissioned by RMC, not the occupant) declared normal conditions using air sampling only — without swabbing HVAC components. The November 12 independent post-remediation test, conducted just 23 days later, found active mold growth confirmed in the A/C intake, directly refuting the October clearance. The A/C intake circulates air throughout the entire unit; confirmed growth there is a whole-unit air quality concern. The current sensor data (beginning March 2026) shows sustained humidity above 70% on —% of all recorded readings — consistent with the chronic moisture conditions that produced and sustained the documented mold events.
